scenes.sceneTitle: Humanity is created in God’s image

presets.text: Who is God speaking to when he says, “Let’s make man in our image”?
What does it mean for humans to be made in God’s image?
Why does the passage say male and female are both created in God’s image?
Why is ruling over the other creatures connected to being made in God’s image?
What does “subdue” the earth mean here?
Why does God give plants and fruit for food to humans and animals?
What changes when God looks at everything he has made and calls it “very good”?

scenes.sceneTitle: The man is formed, placed, and commanded

presets.text: Why does God form the man from dust instead of simply speaking him into existence?
What changes when God breathes the breath of life into the man?
What does it mean for the man to become a living soul?
Why is the man placed in the garden to work and keep it?
Why are the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil both in the garden?
Why is only one tree forbidden when the rest are available for food?
What exactly does “you will surely die” mean if the man does not die immediately after eating?

scenes.sceneTitle: The woman is built and brought to the man

presets.text: Why does God say it is not good for the man to be alone?
Why does God bring the animals to the man before making the woman?
What does it mean that no helper comparable to the man is found among the animals?
Why is the woman made from the man’s own body?
What does “bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh” mean?
Why does the passage connect this scene with a man leaving his parents and joining his wife?
Why are the man and woman naked without being ashamed?

scenes.sceneTitle: The fruit is taken and both eat

presets.text: Why does the serpent begin by questioning what God said?
Why does the woman add “you shall not touch it” when describing God’s command?
Why does the serpent directly contradict the warning that they will die?
What does it mean to know good and evil?
Why does the fruit become desirable only after the serpent’s explanation?
Why does the man eat when he is there with the woman?
Why is nakedness the first thing they notice after eating?

scenes.sceneTitle: The man hides and answers the LORD God

presets.text: Why do the man and woman hide from God after eating?
Why does God ask the man, “Where are you?” if God already knows what happened?
Why does fear become part of the man’s explanation?
Why does the man point to both the woman and God when explaining why he ate?
Why does the woman point to the serpent?
Does either person actually confess wrongdoing in this exchange?
What changed in their relationship with God between the garden before eating and this conversation afterward?

scenes.sceneTitle: Adam hears of ground, toil, dust, and death

presets.text: Why are the serpent, the woman, and Adam addressed separately?
What is the hostility between the serpent’s offspring and the woman’s offspring supposed to describe?
Why does the woman’s judgment focus on childbirth and relationship?
Why is the ground cursed because of Adam?
Why does work become painful if work already existed before the disobedience?
What does returning to dust mean for Adam’s life and death?
Why does Adam name the woman Eve after hearing the judgment about death?
Why does God make clothing for them?

scenes.sceneTitle: The man is sent out and the garden is guarded

presets.text: What does it mean that the man has become “like one of us” in knowing good and evil?
Why is living forever after this point treated as something that must be prevented?
What would eating from the tree of life have done?
Why is the man sent out to work the ground from which he was taken?
Why does God both send the man out and then drive him out?
Why are cherubim and a flaming sword needed to guard the way back?
Is mortality caused by the earlier judgment, by losing access to the tree of life, or by both?

scenes.sceneTitle: Cain and Abel enter Adam’s family story

presets.text: Why does Eve describe Cain’s birth as something she received with the LORD’s help?
Why are Cain and Abel given different kinds of work?
Why does God respect Abel’s offering but not Cain’s?
Does the passage explain what was wrong with Cain’s offering?
Why does God warn Cain that sin is crouching at the door?
What does it mean that sin desires Cain but Cain must rule over it?
Why does Cain kill Abel after being warned?

scenes.sceneTitle: Abel’s death reshapes the family’s ground and place

presets.text: Why does God ask Cain where Abel is after the murder?
What does Cain mean by asking, “Am I my brother’s keeper?”
What does it mean for Abel’s blood to cry from the ground?
Why does Cain’s punishment involve the ground he used to work?
Why is Cain afraid someone will kill him if he becomes a wanderer?
Why does God protect Cain with a sign after Cain killed Abel?
Why does Cain leave the LORD’s presence and settle in Nod?

scenes.sceneTitle: Adam and Eve receive Seth after Abel

presets.text: Why does Eve describe Seth as a replacement for Abel?
How does Seth’s birth change Adam and Eve’s family after Cain and Abel?
Why is Cain mentioned again in the explanation of Seth’s name?
Why does the story move so quickly from Seth’s birth to Enosh?
What does it mean that people began to call on the LORD’s name at this time?
Does the passage explain why this practice begins in Seth’s line?

scenes.sceneTitle: Adam’s generations end with his death

presets.text: Why does the genealogy repeat that humanity was made in God’s likeness?
Why are male and female both included when the name Adam is given?
How is Seth being in Adam’s likeness related to Adam being in God’s likeness?
Why are Adam’s other sons and daughters left unnamed?
Why is Adam’s age given in such detail?
Why does the genealogy end Adam’s entry with the simple statement, “and he died”?
What does Adam’s death say about the earlier warning that he would die?

scenes.sceneTitle: Chronicles begins its genealogy with Adam

presets.text: Why does Chronicles begin its genealogy with Adam?
Why are Adam, Seth, and Enosh named with no stories attached?
What is gained by tracing the line from Adam all the way to Noah in just a few names?
Why does Chronicles include this ancient ancestry before turning to Israel’s later history?
Does this list treat Adam mainly as a person, an ancestor, or both?

scenes.sceneTitle: Luke traces Jesus back to Adam and God

presets.text: Why does Luke trace Jesus’ family line all the way back to Adam?
Why does the genealogy continue one step beyond Adam to God?
What does calling Adam the son of God mean here?
Why does Luke place this genealogy immediately before Jesus is tested?
How does tracing Jesus to Adam change the scope of the story compared with a genealogy that stops with Abraham?
Is Luke saying Jesus is related to all humanity through Adam, or is the genealogy doing something more?

scenes.sceneTitle: Jude calls Enoch the seventh from Adam

presets.text: Why does Jude identify Enoch as the seventh from Adam?
What does Adam contribute to Jude’s argument if he is only being used to locate Enoch?
Why does Jude quote Enoch in a warning about judgment?
What does the repeated word “ungodly” add to the warning?
Why are speech, desire, complaining, and flattery all grouped together in the description of these people?
Does Jude’s reference to Adam tell us anything about Adam himself beyond genealogy?

scenes.sceneTitle: Job asks whether he hid wrong like Adam

presets.text: What does Job mean by saying he did not cover his transgressions like Adam?
Is Job referring to Adam hiding in the garden, blaming others, or something else?
Why does hiding wrongdoing become part of Job’s defense of his own integrity?
What does this comparison assume the reader already knows about Adam?
Does this verse treat Adam mainly as the first sinner, as someone who hid sin, or both?

scenes.sceneTitle: Hosea compares covenant breach to Adam

presets.text: What covenant does Hosea mean when he says the people broke covenant like Adam?
Does Genesis ever explicitly call God’s command to Adam a covenant?
Why does Hosea compare Israel’s unfaithfulness with Adam’s?
What does “there they were unfaithful to me” refer to?
Is Adam being used as one example of covenant breaking, or as the beginning of a larger pattern?

scenes.sceneTitle: Wisdom links death with the devil’s envy

presets.text: What does it mean to say humanity was created for incorruption?
How is being made in God’s image connected with immortality in this passage?
Why does Wisdom say death entered the world through the devil’s envy?
How does this explanation of death compare with the Genesis account of Adam and Eve?
Who are the people said to belong to the devil and experience death?
Is this passage explaining physical death, moral death, or something broader?

scenes.sceneTitle: Sirach says sin began from a woman

presets.text: Why does Sirach say sin began from a woman?
How does that claim fit with Genesis, where both the woman and the man eat?
Why does Sirach say that because of her everyone dies?
Is this passage blaming Eve specifically, women generally, or using Eve as part of a warning about marriage?
Why does the surrounding passage speak so harshly about women?
How should a reader distinguish Sirach’s later interpretation from what Genesis itself says?

scenes.sceneTitle: Tobias remembers Adam and Eve while praying

presets.text: Why do Tobias and Sarah bring Adam and Eve into their wedding prayer?
What does it mean for Eve to be Adam’s helper and support here?
Why does Tobias say human descendants came from Adam and Eve as part of asking for mercy?
Why does Tobias say he is marrying Sarah in truth rather than for lust?
How does this prayer use Adam and Eve as a model for marriage?
Does this later portrait simplify the more complicated relationship shown in Genesis?

scenes.sceneTitle: Sirach remembers Adam formed from dust

presets.text: Why does Sirach begin this reflection by saying all people come from the ground and Adam came from dust?
How does Adam’s creation from dust support the comparison with clay in a potter’s hand?
Why does the passage say God makes some people different from others?
How can blessing, cursing, life, death, light, and darkness all be placed in paired opposites?
What part of human life is being compared with the potter shaping clay?
Does this passage leave any room for human choice, or does it emphasize only God’s control?

scenes.sceneTitle: The sons of Adam share toil and mortality

presets.text: Why does Sirach describe life under a heavy yoke from birth to burial?
Why are all of Adam’s descendants included, from kings to people in poverty?
Why is fear of death described as something that troubles human thought?
What does calling burial a return to the mother of all things mean?
How is this picture of human life connected to Adam’s story?
Does Sirach treat toil and mortality as universal consequences of being human?

scenes.sceneTitle: Sirach places Adam above other remembered people

presets.text: Why does Sirach say Adam is above every living thing in creation?
What makes Adam’s status different from Enoch, Joseph, Shem, and Seth in this list?
Is Adam being praised for his character here, or for his unique place in creation?
Why are Enoch, Joseph, Shem, Seth, and Adam grouped together in this closing remembrance?
What does this later tradition remember about Adam that Genesis does not say in those words?

scenes.sceneTitle: Adam is formed, enlivened, led, and judged

presets.text: Why does this prayer describe Adam as a body without a soul before God breathes life into him?
How does the breath of life change Adam in this retelling?
Why is Adam’s command described as the one commandment?
What does the prayer mean by saying death was appointed immediately after Adam transgressed?
How does this retelling connect Adam’s personal transgression with the deaths of his descendants?
Why does the prayer compare Adam’s generation with the generation destroyed by the flood?
Which parts of this retelling go beyond the wording of Genesis itself?

scenes.sceneTitle: Adam’s wicked heart is traced through later generations

presets.text: Why does this prayer call Adam the first transgressor?
What is the “wicked heart” the prayer says remained even after God gave the law?
How is Adam’s disobedience connected with the later failures of Israel?
Why does the prayer say the law could not remove the wicked heart?
Why are Abraham and Sinai placed inside an argument that begins with Adam?
Is the problem in this passage something inherited from Adam, repeated by each generation, or both?
Why does the prayer say Jerusalem’s people did what Adam and all his generations had done?

scenes.sceneTitle: Evil seed is said to grow from Adam’s heart

presets.text: What does it mean to say an evil seed was sown in Adam’s heart?
Who or what sowed that evil seed?
Why does the passage describe wickedness as something that grows and produces fruit over time?
How does Adam’s heart become connected with the wickedness of later generations?
What is the “harvest” or “time of threshing” that has not yet come?
Does this passage describe evil as inherited, copied, or simply multiplied through history?

scenes.sceneTitle: Adam is remembered as ruler and ancestor

presets.text: Why is Adam remembered as ruler over creation in this prayer?
If all nations come from Adam, why does the prayer treat Israel as different from the other nations?
Why does the speaker say the world was made for Israel’s sake?
How can nations described as almost nothing end up ruling over God’s chosen people?
Why does Adam’s place at the beginning of humanity matter to this complaint about Israel’s present suffering?
What does the speaker expect God to do because Israel comes from the same Adam but is also called God’s firstborn?

scenes.sceneTitle: The world’s narrow way is linked to Adam

presets.text: How does Adam’s transgression make the whole world narrow, sorrowful, and difficult?
Why should people born long after Adam live in a world changed by what he did?
What does the passage mean when it says this condition was decreed when Adam transgressed?
Why is Israel’s present struggle explained by going all the way back to Adam?
Does this passage describe Adam’s act as changing human life, the world itself, or both?
Does the passage explain exactly how Adam’s transgression produced these conditions?

scenes.sceneTitle: Judgment is said to be prepared with Adam

presets.text: Why does the passage say everyone born is already full of sin and transgression?
How is that condition connected to Adam?
Why would judgment be prepared when God made Adam and his descendants?
Does preparing judgment that early mean God expected humanity to fail?
Why does the speaker think life might be better if there were no judgment after death?
How are personal sins and Adam’s place at the beginning of humanity being held together here?

scenes.sceneTitle: The speaker laments what Adam’s sin brought

presets.text: Why does the speaker wish Adam had never been created?
Why does he wish God had restrained Adam from sinning?
If Adam was responsible for his own sin, why does the speaker ask why God did not stop him?
How does the evil from Adam’s sin fall on everyone who comes from him?
Why are later people said to suffer for something Adam did before they were born?
Is the speaker blaming Adam, blaming human nature, questioning God, or doing all three?
Does the passage explain how Adam’s act affects his descendants, or only insist that it does?

scenes.sceneTitle: Romans traces sin and death through one man

presets.text: How does sin entering through one man lead to death reaching everyone?
What does Paul mean by saying death spread to everyone because all sinned?
How can sin exist before the law if sin is not charged where there is no law?
Why does death still reign over people who did not sin in the same way Adam did?
What was different about Adam’s disobedience compared with the sins of people after him?
Why does Paul call Adam a pattern of someone who was still to come?
Does Paul say people die only because Adam sinned, only because they sin, or somehow because of both?

scenes.sceneTitle: Adam’s trespass is set beside Christ’s gift

presets.text: How can one person’s trespass bring death and condemnation to many people?
How can one person’s obedience make many people righteous?
Why does Paul say the gift is not simply equal to the trespass but much greater?
What does it mean for death to reign through Adam’s trespass?
What does it mean for people receiving grace to reign in life?
Why does Paul say the law came in so that the trespass would increase?
How can increasing sin become the setting in which grace increases even more?
When Paul says one trespass led to condemnation for all and one righteous act led to life for all, who does “all” include in each statement?

scenes.sceneTitle: Death in Adam stands beside life in Christ

presets.text: What does it mean to say that everyone dies in Adam?
How does being made alive in Christ answer what happened in Adam?
Why is Christ called the firstfruits of those who have died?
Why does resurrection happen in an order rather than all at once?
Why must Christ reign until every enemy is under his feet?
Why is death called the last enemy?
What happens to death when it is finally abolished?
Why does the Son become subject to God after everything else has been subjected to him?

scenes.sceneTitle: First and last Adam frame two kinds of embodied life

presets.text: What kind of body does Paul think people will have when they are raised?
Why does Paul compare resurrection to a seed that dies before a new body appears?
What is the difference between a natural body and a spiritual body?
How can a body be both truly embodied and still be called spiritual?
Why does Paul call Adam the first man and Christ the last Adam?
What does it mean that Adam became a living soul while the last Adam became a life-giving spirit?
Why does Paul connect Adam with dust and Christ with heaven?
What does it mean to bear the image of the earthly and then the image of the heavenly?
Does Paul expect the raised person to be the same body transformed, or an entirely different kind of body?

scenes.sceneTitle: The letter distinguishes formation and deception

presets.text: Why does the order in which Adam and Eve were formed become part of an instruction about teaching and authority?
Why does the passage say Adam was not deceived even though he still disobeyed?
What difference is the writer drawing between being deceived and knowingly disobeying?
Why is Eve’s deception used to support a rule about women in this passage?
What does it mean that a woman will be saved through childbearing?
Who are the people meant by “if they continue in faith, love, and holiness”?
Is this instruction tied only to the situation being addressed here, or is it intended more broadly?
How should Adam’s role in Genesis be understood when this passage says the woman, not Adam, was deceived?
